summary: Poverty Island Light, Michigan: a brick tower lit in 1874-75 at the Poverty Island Passage into Green Bay; automated in the 1950s and deactivated.

light.note: A temporary fixed white light was first shown 1 August 1874; the tower's lantern room was first lit 10 August 1875 (LighthouseFriends). The 1875 focal plane was 78 ft (LighthouseFriends); the USLHS record gives 80 ft above mean high water.

lens.note: Fourth-order Fresnel lens, 1875. Replaced by a 36-inch revolving light in 1952 (LighthouseFriends). USLHS record: current optic none.

structures.note: 70 ft (21 m) from base to centre of lantern (USLHS record). Connected to the dwelling by a covered passage (LighthouseFriends). Lantern room removed by 1965.
One-story bungalow with basement and porch, 24½ by 42½ ft (7.5 by 13 m), begun 23 October 1920 (LighthouseFriends; Commissioner FY1922).
Frame building covered and lined with sheet iron; water from an offshore crib (LighthouseFriends).
Circular iron oil house, September 1894 (Light-House Board FY1895).

access.note: Reached only by boat. Grounds and tower closed (LighthouseFriends). Not open to the public (USLHS record).

events.note: Construction of the tower begins 28 August 1873, after Congress appropriated $18,000 on 3 March 1873 (LighthouseFriends).
Fire on 25 October 1873 destroys the workers' sleeping shanties and some materials (LighthouseFriends).
Temporary fixed white light from a sixth-order lens in a lantern on the dwelling roof, 1 August 1874 (LighthouseFriends).
Tower lantern room first lit 10 August 1875 (LighthouseFriends).
Fourth-order Fresnel lens, flashing red at a focal plane of 78 ft (LighthouseFriends). USLHS record: original optic fourth order, installed 1874.
Retaining wall built around the footing and foundation courses to stop settling; tower badly cracked by faulty construction (LighthouseFriends).
Fog-signal building begun 15 August 1885; 10-inch steam whistle first used 15 October 1885 (LighthouseFriends). USLHS record: fog-signal building 1885.
A second assistant keeper is added to the station (LighthouseFriends).
Circular iron oil house erected September 1894; a boat landing built in an L shape to form a harbor for the keeper's boat (Light-House Board FY1895).
Intensity raised to 1,900 candlepower with an incandescent oil-vapor lamp, 24 April 1916 (LighthouseFriends; Lighthouse Service Bulletin 1916).
Steam whistle replaced by an air diaphone, powered by oil-engine compressors (Lighthouse Service Bulletin 1921; LighthouseFriends).
Keeper's bungalow completed; work began 23 October 1920 (LighthouseFriends); the 1922 report describes it (Commissioner of Lighthouses FY1922).
Main light, fog signal and dwelling electrified; fourth-order lens replaced by a 36-inch revolving light (LighthouseFriends).
USLHS record gives 1957. LighthouseFriends says 1958 (see the 1958 entry).
LighthouseFriends: the station was automated in 1958.
Lantern room removed from the top of the tower by 1965, leaving an automated light (LighthouseFriends).
USLHS record gives the year discontinued as about 1990.
LighthouseFriends: deactivated in 1995. The record and the USLHS record differ (see notes).

corrections.why: LighthouseFriends: the tower's lantern room was first lit 10 August 1875; the 1874 light was a temporary one on the dwelling roof. The USLHS record gives 1874 for the tower's establishment, so the editor should choose.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The record and the USLHS record give 1874. LighthouseFriends: a temporary fixed white light was first shown on 1 August 1874 from the dwelling roof, and the tower's lantern was first lit 10 August 1875. The story gives both dates, and facts.light.first_lit is kept at 1874 for the temporary light.
USLHS: original fourth-order optic installed 1874. LighthouseFriends: the 1874 temporary light used a sixth-order lens; the fourth-order Fresnel lens was used when the tower was first lit in 1875.

notes_for_editor: 1) NRHP 05000984: the nomination PDF is not digitised at NPS (the placeholder reads 'The PDF file for this National Register record has not yet been digitized.'), so nothing is cited from it. The 2005 listing year (record; Wikipedia lead only) is unverified. 2) Deactivation year conflicts: record 1976 (Rowlett's Directory, not read); USLHS record 'Year Discontinued: C.1990'; LighthouseFriends 1995. Unresolved; the events list keeps both the USLHS and LighthouseFriends dates. 3) Automation: USLHS record 1957; LighthouseFriends 1958. Both kept as events. 4) Lantern removal: LighthouseFriends says the lantern room was removed by 1965. A USLHS search snippet (the cached place page does not include the history) gives 1976 for the lens and lantern removal and says the tower was sealed; not read in full, not used. 5) Sand Point lantern: LighthouseFriends says the discarded Poverty Island lantern room was placed atop the restored Sand Point Lighthouse; the Delta County Historical Society page says a duplicate cast-iron lantern room from Poverty Island completed the restoration. The editor should check whether the Sand Point lantern is the original. 6) Focal height: LighthouseFriends gives a 78 ft focal plane (1875); the USLHS record gives 80 ft above mean high water (the record's 24.4 m). The facts carry 23.8 m with the note. 7) Keepers: 84 lines from the USLHS roster, normalised by roster.py. Roles: head keeper, acting keeper, first and second assistant, laborer, and 'other' for five Coast Guard lines whose positions are not stated (role_note kept). Spans printed 'at least' or open-ended are kept as printed in the note and carry from_approx or to_approx where the roster marks them. 8) Lighthouse Board fog-signal hours: FY1894 entry 1378 and FY1895 entry 1440 are cited by entry number (printed page not confirmed); FY1896 entry 1558 is on p. 126 (the printed header before it). 9) Commissioner of Lighthouses FY1920 p. 53 and FY1922 pp. 42 and 49 are from the corpus's printed-page reading. The FY1922 dwelling dimensions are OCR'd as '24$ by 42$' and were checked against LighthouseFriends's wording, 'twenty-four-and-half feet by forty-two-and-a-half feet'. 10) A Light-House Board report entry for 'Poverty Island, Wisconsin' (FY1893 volume, entry 1336, whistle 156 hours) names a Poverty Island in Wisconsin. None of the sources read gives a Wisconsin light of that name. It is probably a misprint for the Michigan light, but it could be a different island. Not used. 11) Incidents from LighthouseFriends with no primary source found: the 1884 Oscar Townsend grounding (a newspaper quoted by LighthouseFriends), McCormick's July 1912 launch fire (the Escanaba Morning Press, as quoted), Lee's June 1923 death and Johnson's voyage (LighthouseFriends cites a Manitowoc Herald obituary and a 1987 book), and Jensen's October 1936 death. Chronicling America searches for Michigan 1912-1915 and Wisconsin 1923, and general 1912-1936 terms, returned no matching pages. The story attributes these to LighthouseFriends. The editor should verify before publication. 12) The story does not name the children of the keepers' families, and it does not repeat LighthouseFriends's anecdote from a 1987 book about a former keeper's child, because the people may be living and the anecdote is second-hand. 13) Benjamin F. Johnson: the roster has him as second assistant 1921-1923 and first assistant 1923-1936. LighthouseFriends says he began in 1921 and was promoted to first assistant on Lee's death in 1923; consistent. 14) William A. Goudreau: the roster gives second assistant 1939-1949; LighthouseFriends (a son's recollection) says the late 1930s. Not reconciled. 15) Wikipedia (lead only, not cited): listed on the NRHP in 2005. Not used. 16) Ownership: LighthouseFriends says the Coast Guard owns the lighthouse; the record's agency field should be checked against the current Coast Guard List of Lights. The USLHS record reports it is not an active aid and not a private aid. 17) Characteristic: the record has no characteristic. The 1875 light was flashing red (LighthouseFriends). The current characteristic was not found in the sources read, so the facts keep the 1875 description only. 18) Fact-check pass 2026-10-27: each footnoted sentence was checked against LighthouseFriends, the USLHS place record, the Light-House Board volumes (FY1894 entry 1378; FY1895 entry 1440; FY1896 entry 1558 on p. 126, header confirmed), the Commissioner of Lighthouses volume (FY1920 p. 53; FY1922 pp. 42 and 49, printed pages confirmed by the OCR index), the Lighthouse Service Bulletins (1916 PDF p. 22; 1921 PDF p. 47) and the Delta County Historical Society page. Changes made to the story: the roster sentence was garbled (it ran Peterson and Messer together out of order); it now cites the first roster line only. 'Lighthouse Service record' is now the U.S. Lighthouse Society place record (three places). Lantern room: LighthouseFriends says the Society was given permission to restore the discarded lantern room; the Society's page calls the lantern on Sand Point 'a duplicate cast iron lantern room from Poverty Island'. The story reports both and says the sources do not agree on whether it is the original. Lee: the first draft said his wife and children had come over; LighthouseFriends says he went to fetch them, and that Johnson later returned to pick them up. Corrected. 1916: the Bulletin records the change of illuminant only; the candlepower figure is LighthouseFriends', and both are cited. 1919 act: the FY1920 report says an allotment of $6,500 was made under the act, not that the Service 'set aside' a sum; corrected. Atmosphere: 'swept through' is now 'broke out' with the date given; 'the light can be seen from excursion boats' is now LighthouseFriends' 'excursions ... may be offered'; 'The island is reached by boat' is removed. Still unverified: the printed pages of the FY1894 (entry 1378) and FY1895 (entry 1440) Light-House Board entries (the corpus has no page index for them), and the lantern room's original status.
